title: Microwave spectroscopic study of malonaldehyde (3-hydroxy-2-propenal). 2. Structure, dipole moment, and tunneling
authors: Steven L. Baughcum; Richard W. Duerst; Walter F. Rowe; Zuzana Smith; E. Bright Wilson
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society 103(21), 6296–6303
note: Historical microwave spectroscopy links molecular structure and hydrogen-transfer tunneling. The full historical paper was not obtained; no new spectral fit is claimed.

title: Full-dimensional quantum calculations of ground-state tunneling splitting of malonaldehyde using an accurate ab initio potential energy surface
authors: Yimin Wang; Bastiaan J. Braams; Joel M. Bowman; Stuart Carter; David P. Tew
note: A full-dimensional surface fitted to 11,147 near-basis-limit CCSD(T) energies has a reported saddle barrier of 4.1 kcal/mol. That is a different protocol, not a matched-geometry error bar for our PBE path.

title: A compact and accurate semi-global potential energy surface for malonaldehyde from constrained least squares regression
authors: Wataru Mizukami; Scott Habershon; David P. Tew
note: Constrained least-squares/LASSO fitting of explicitly correlated coupled-cluster energies supports full-dimensional diffusion Monte Carlo. The reported H/D splittings illustrate the separate roles of PES and nuclear solution.

title: The hydrogen tunneling splitting in malonaldehyde: A full-dimensional time-independent quantum mechanical method
authors: Feng Wu; Yinghui Ren; Wensheng Bian
note: A full-dimensional time-independent calculation studies coupled vibrational modes. Our observed O–O contraction is a path geometry result, not an equivalent mode-resolved tunneling calculation.

title: Transfer Learning for Affordable and High-Quality Tunneling Splittings from Instanton Calculations
authors: Silvan Käser; Jeremy O. Richardson; Markus Meuwly
journal: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation 18(11), 6840–6850
note: 25–50 high-level structures refine an already trained MP2 surface around the instanton path. This is not learning an accurate global potential from 25 total structures.
access: Primary abstract and indexed supporting information

title: The exact tunnelling splitting of malonaldehyde from symmetrized path-integral molecular dynamics
authors: Jonah Baumann; George Trenins; Jeremy O. Richardson
note: Symmetrized path integrals isolate the ground rotational state; the reported 21.1 ± 0.1 cm⁻¹ is exact in the convergence limit for a specified PES, not for every electronic-structure approximation.
access: Author-repository abstract and selected publisher text

title: Tests Demonstrate the Accuracy of the Qim-Reaction Path Hamiltonian for Double-Well Tunneling Splittings for H-Atom Transfer
authors: Chen Qu; Apurba Nandi; Paul L. Houston; Joel M. Bowman
note: The Qim reaction-path Hamiltonian tests show that a one-dimensional reduction must be judged by its coordinate, kinetic operator and benchmarks, rather than rejected merely for being one-dimensional.
access: Primary abstract and publisher methods excerpt

title: Generalized Gradient Approximation Made Simple
authors: John P. Perdew; Kieron Burke; Matthias Ernzerhof
note: PBE is a specified semilocal exchange-correlation approximation. Agreement with that reference is not a measurement of experimental accuracy.

title: Insights into current limitations of density functional theory
authors: Aron J. Cohen; Paula Mori-Sánchez; Weitao Yang
note: Delocalization and static-correlation errors explain important DFT limitations in general. They do not diagnose the cause of this project’s barrier without matched calculations.

title: Moment Tensor Potentials: A Class of Systematically Improvable Interatomic Potentials
note: Moment tensor potentials form a systematically improvable invariant model family for approximating a chosen quantum interaction model. Systematic form is not a guarantee for one trained model.

title: Active learning of linearly parametrized interatomic potentials
authors: Evgeny V. Podryabinkin; Alexander V. Shapeev
note: D-optimality guides selection in the space of model equations. A design with K equal to the whole candidate pool does not test competitive subset ranking.

title: Forces Are Not Enough: Benchmark and Critical Evaluation for Machine Learning Force Fields with Molecular Simulations
authors: Xiang Fu; Zhenghao Wu; Wujie Wang; Tian Xie; Sinan Keten; Rafael Gómez-Bombarelli; Tommi Jaakkola
note: Force/energy prediction error and realistic molecular simulation are distinct evaluation targets. Stability and simulation observables deserve separate checks.

title: A climbing image nudged elastic band method for finding saddle points and minimum energy paths
authors: Graeme Henkelman; Blas Pedro Uberuaga; Hannes Jónsson
note: Climbing-image NEB locates a saddle along a minimum-energy path. Saved path images are not equally spaced times on a reaction trajectory.

title: Reactive Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials for Chemistry and Materials Science
authors: Jisu Kim; Hyunsung Cho; Haekwan Jeon; Jisu Jung; Seungwu Han
note: A contemporary review separates model architecture from acquisition of reactive training data. It situates this small MTP study without validating its generalization.

title: Animated Transitions in Statistical Data Graphics
journal: IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics 13(6), 1240–1247
note: Staged transitions help viewers track graphic changes; the source motivates stable identities and fixed axes, not constant motion.

title: Effectiveness of Animation in Trend Visualization
authors: George Robertson; Roland Fernandez; Danyel Fisher; Bongshin Lee; John Stasko
journal: IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics 14(6), 1325–1332
note: Animation can attract attention while underperforming static alternatives on analytic tasks. Every guided sequence here leaves an inspectable static comparison.

title: Narrative Visualization: Telling Stories with Data
journal: IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics 16(6), 1139–1148
note: Narrative structure and reader-driven exploration can coexist. The site pairs a short guided sequence with exact-state inspection.

title: The misuse of colour in science communication
authors: Fabio Crameri; Grace E. Shephard; Philip J. Heron
note: Perceptually uneven or inaccessible colors can distort scientific communication. Direct labels and line styles supplement the consistent categorical palette.

title: MolViewStories: Interactive molecular storytelling
authors: Terézia Slanináková; Zachary Charlop-Powers; Viktoriia Doshchenko; Alexander S. Rose; Adam Midlik; Anna Sekuła; Neli Fonseca; Kyle L. Morris; Stephen K. Burley; Sameer Velankar; Jennifer Fleming; Brinda Vallat; Ludovic Autin; David Sehnal
note: Reproducible scene specifications link structures, narrative and motion. This site adopts that architectural principle, not the full macromolecular software stack.
